## Source: amazon-inspector (46dc181d726e4b49d0bcc688f5fe6518c515d7ba8c9153f2c973e5aa33cb830c)
On require(), index.js reconstructs the module name 'child_process' by XOR-decoding a hex blob against a repeating 0x42 key, locates a Bun runtime at /usr/local/bin/bun or ~/.bun/bin/bun, writes a JS file to the OS temp directory (p<timestamp>.js), and spawns Bun against that file. The written file is currently empty, so no payload executes today, but the full dropper scaffolding — obfuscated child_process import, alternate-runtime discovery, tmp-file write, spawn — is wired to the module's top-level load path. Legitimate utility libraries do not need to conceal the identity of 'child_process' from static scanners, and the shape (obfuscated primitive + write-and-exec via a sibling runtime at import time) matches the npm alternate-runtime dropper pattern.
